Bug_Title: Regex boundaries should not be used in a way that can never be matched
Bug_Details:
In regular expressions the boundaries ^ and \A can only match at the beginning of the input (or, in case of ^ in combination with the MULTILINE flag, the beginning of the line) and $ , \Z and \z only at the end.
These patterns can be misused, by accidentally switching ^ and $ for example, to create a pattern that can never
match.
Noncompliant code example
// This can never match because $ and ^ have been switched around
Pattern.compile("$[a-z]+^"); // Noncompliant
Compliant solution
Pattern.compile("^[a-z]+$");
Bug_Explanation: The regex pattern uses boundaries '$' and '^' in a way that can never match any input. '$' is meant for the end of the input, and '^' is for the start. By placing them in the wrong positions ('$' at the start and '^' at the end), the pattern is rendered unmatchable as it expects a line to simultaneously start and end with letters, which is impossible.
Trigger_Explanation: The test cases use the method showBug with various inputs, expecting it to return true, but due to the incorrect regex pattern '$[a-z]+^', they will always return false. The bug is triggered when assertTrue is used since the pattern can never match any input.
